name: Sibe (Nasioi)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog lists only subclassification notes (Onishi 2004, Evans 2009); no grammar/phonology of Sibe (Nasioi group) found

sources.citation: Teramura, Hiroshi 寺村裕史 & Kazuya Inagaki. 2011. GISを用いた方言分布の地理的分析—南ブーゲンヴィルのシベ(ナゴヴィシ)語の方言地図. 地球研言語記述論集 3: 183-208.
sources.note: Dialect-geography of lexical/phonological variables; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Inagaki, Kazuya 稲垣和也. 2010. ナゴヴィシ・シベ語の類別詞 [Classifiers in Nagovisi-Sibe]. 地球研言語記述論集 (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series) 2: 135-163.
sources.note: Sec. 1.2 (pp. 137-138) gives 5 short vowels, 7 long vowels, 14 consonants, glottal stop distribution and dialect differences; says nothing about stress or accent (no アクセント/強勢/声調 anywhere in the paper).
sources.venue: 地球研言語記述論集 (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series)

sources.citation: Regan, Anthony J. & Helga M. Griffin (eds). 2005. Bougainville before the conflict. Canberra: Pandanus Books (incl. D. Tryon, 'The languages of Bougainville').
sources.note: Overview/classification and language names only (Nagovisi = Sibbe/Sibee/Tobee); nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Onishi, Masayuki. 1994. A grammar of Motuna (Bougainville, Papua New Guinea). PhD thesis, ANU. (checked only for Nagovisi references)
sources.note: Describes Motuna, not Sibe; cites Gasaway 1987a-c and Hunt & Hunt 1972 'Nagovisi phonemes' / 1973 'Nagovisi verb paper' (SIL mss) as the Nagovisi phonological sources; no statement about Nagovisi stress.

sources.citation: Nash, Jill. 1974. Matriliny and modernisation: the Nagovisi of South Bougainville. New Guinea Research Bulletin 55. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Anthropology; p. 5 note that the language (Sibbe) is close to Nasioi; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG (compiler not named on the record). n.d. [issued 2011-09-13]. Nagovisi Organised Phonology Data. Manuscript, 3 pp., draft posted 'as is'. Ukarumpa: SIL Papua New Guinea. SIL Language & Culture Archives (REAP) entry 42243; mirrored record at pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/archives/42243.

tone.summary: Short SIL phonology data sheet; the suprasegmentals paragraph says only that stress is non-phonemic (initial on disyllables); tone is never mentioned beyond the template heading.
